questions.q:
The bob of a simple pendulum has mass $2g$ and a charge of $5.0\muC .$ It is at rest in a uniform horizontal electric field of intensity $2000V / m$ At equilibrium, the angle that the pendulum makes with the vertical is:
\left(takeg = 10m / s^{2}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$tan \theta = \dfrac{QE}{mg} = \dfrac{5 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 2000}{2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$⇒ \theta = \tan^{- 1} \left(0.5\right)$

questions.q: Two charges $7 \mu \mathrm{c}$ and $-4 \mu \mathrm{c}$ are placed at $(-7 \mathrm{~cm}, 0,0)$ and $(7 \mathrm{~cm}, 0,0)$ respectively. Given, $\epsilon_0=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}^2 \mathrm{~N}^{-1} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$, the electrostatic potential energy of the charge configuration is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
P.E. of two charges
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{u}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{\mathrm{q}_1 \mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{r}} \\
& \mathrm{r}=\sqrt{\left(\mathrm{x}_2-\mathrm{x}_1\right)^2+\left(\mathrm{y}_2-\mathrm{y}_1\right)^2+\left(\mathrm{z}_2-\mathrm{z}_1\right)^2} \\
& =14 \mathrm{~cm} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{u}=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 7 \times 10^{-6} \times(-4) \times 10^{-6}}{14 \times 10^{-2}} \\
& =-1.8 \mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$

At $5$ cm from $20\muC$ on the left side of system

questions.solution:
Charge should be placed near $- 5\muC$ at $x$ distance

$\dfrac{K ( 20 ) Q}{( 5 + x{)}^{2}} = \dfrac{K ( 5 ) Q}{X2}$
$4x^{2} = ( 5 + x{)}^{2}$
$4x^{2} = 25 + x^{2} + 10x$
$3x^{2} - 10x - 25 = 0$~$⇒ x = 5$

questions.q:
A charge $Q$ is distributed over three concentric spherical shells of radii $a, b, c \left(a < b < c\right)$ such that their surface charge densities are equal to one another.

The total potential at a point at distance $r$ from their common centre, where $r < a, would be:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Surface charge densities of all sphere is given as& $\dfrac{{q}_{1}}{a^{2}} = \dfrac{{q}_{2}}{b^{2}} = \dfrac{{q}_{3}}{c^{2}} = constant$, where~${q}_{1}$,~${q}_{2}$~and~${q}_{3}$~is charge on sphere of radius~$a$,~$b$~and~$c$~respectively.

${q}_{1} + {q}_{2} + {q}_{3} = Q$

${q}_{1} = \dfrac{a^{2} ( Q )}{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}$

${q}_{2} = \dfrac{b^{2} ( Q )}{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}$

${q}_{3} = \dfrac{c^{2}\left(Q\right)}{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}$

Potential at a point where~$r < a$~is given as~$V = \dfrac{K{q}_{1}}{a} + \dfrac{K{q}_{2}}{b} + \dfrac{K{q}_{3}}{c}$, where~$K$~is a constant.

$V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \left[$Q\right]\left(\dfrac{a + b + c}{a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}})$

$

The electric field at the middle point $O$ between the charges is $6 . 4 \times {10}^{4}NC^{- 1}$. The distance '$d$' between the point charges $A$ and $B$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Direction of electric field at mid-point due to both charge will be in same direction, which is towards right.

Therefore,& $E$~at mid-point~$= \dfrac{kq}{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)2} + \dfrac{kq}{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)2}$~

$⇒ 6 . 4 \times {10}^{4} = 2 \times \left[9 \times {10}^{9} \times \left($8 $\times {10}^{- 6}\right)$d^{2} \times4\right]$

$⇒ d = 3m$

$

questions.q: A solid conducting sphere, having a charge $Q,$ is surrounded by an uncharged conducting hollow spherical shell. Let the potential difference between the surface of the solid sphere and that of the outer surface of the hollow shell be $V .$ If the shell is now given a charge of $– 4Q,$ the new potential difference between the same two surfaces is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
First condition:

Both conducting spheres are shown.
${V}_{in} - {V}_{out} = $\left(\dfrac{KQ}{r1}) -\left(\dfrac{KQ}{r2})$
$⇒ V = KQ \left(\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}}\right)$
Second condition:

Shell is now given charge $- 4Q$ .
${V}_{in} - {V}_{out} = \left(\dfrac{KQ}{{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{4KQ}{{r}_{2}}) - $\left(\dfrac{KQ}{{r}_{2}} - \dfrac{4KQ}{{r}_{2}})
=\dfrac{KQ}{{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{KQ}{{r}_{2}}
=KQ\left(\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}}) =V$

In the second configuration (2), the same charges are shifted to mid points ($\mathrm{G}, \mathrm{E}, \mathrm{H}$) and F, of the square, If ($\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}$), the difference between the potential energies of configuration (2) and (1) is given by :$

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& u_{\oplus}=\left(2 \frac{K q_0}{a}+\frac{K q_0}{\sqrt{2} a}\right) q_0 \times 2 \\
& u_0=\left(2 \frac{K q_0 \sqrt{2}}{a}+\frac{K q_0}{a}\right) q_0 \times 2
\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned}
& \text { So, } \quad \Delta u=u_2-u_1=2 q_0 \frac{k q_0}{a}\left[2 \sqrt{2}+1-2-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \Delta u=\frac{2 q_0^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a}\left[\frac{4-\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]=\frac{2 q_0^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a} \frac{(3-\sqrt{2})}{\sqrt{2}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \Delta u=\frac{2 k q_0^2}{a}\left[\frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}\right]=\frac{k q_0^2}{a}(3 \sqrt{2}-2)

questions.q:
Statement-I : A point charge is brought in an electric field. The value of electric field at a point near to the charge may increase if the charge is positive.

Statement-II : An electric dipole is placed in a uniform electric field. The net electric force on the dipole will not be zero.
options: Both statement-I and statement-II are true.
Both statement-I and statement-II are false.
Statement-I is true but statement-II is false.
Statement-I is false but statement-II is true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If a positive point charge is brought in an electric field. The value of electric field at a point near to the charge may increase or decreases. Hence, statement I is true.

An electric dipole experiences zero net force in a uniform electric field. Hence, statement II is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the conservation of energy,
$\dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{q^{2}}{\sqrt{{\left(3a\right)}^{2} + {\left(4a\right)}^{2}}} + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{0}}\dfrac{q^{2}}{\left(3a\right)}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{m}}{\left(\dfrac{2}{15}\dfrac{q^{2}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}a}\right)}^{1 / 2}$

questions.q: Graphical variation of electric field due to a uniformly charged insulating solid sphere of radius $R,$with distance $r$ from the centre $O$ is represented by:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The electric field inside a solid insulated sphere is given by&

${E}_{inside} = \dfrac{ρr}{3{ε}_{0}}$~for~$r < R$~where~$ρ$~is~volume~charge density.

Hence,~the electric field varies linearly with the distance as

${E}_{inside} ∝ r^{1}$

Now, the electric field for~$r > R$~is given by~

${E}_{outside} = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi{ε}_{0}r^{2}}$

${E}_{outside} ∝ \dfrac{1}{r2}$

Thus, the graph starts decreasing as a power law graph as shown in the figure for the region~$r > R$.

Hence, this graph is the right option.

The angle of the deviation \left(θ\right)$ of the path of the electron as it comes out of the field will be _____ .

$

questions.solution:
Time taken by the electron to cross will be,& $t = \dfrac{1}{vx} = \dfrac{1}{2}s$.

Acceleration of the electron along~$y$~axis

${a}_{g} = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{Ee}{m} = \dfrac{8m}{e} \times \dfrac{e}{m} = 8ms^{- 2}$

${v}_{y}$~of the electron~ when it has crossed the capacitor will be,

${v}_{y} = {a}_{y}t = 8 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 4ms^{- 1}$

Therefore,

$tan\theta = \dfrac{vy}{vx} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2 ⇒ \theta = \tan^{- 1} \left(2\right)

$

questions.q:
A particle of mass $1$ mg and charge $q$ is lying at the mid-point of two stationary particles kept at a distance $2m$~when each is carrying same charge $q$. If the free charged particle is displaced from its equilibrium position through distance $x$~ \left(x < < 1m\right)$. The particle executes SHM. Its angular frequency of oscillation will be _______~$\times {10}^{5}rads^{- 1}$~(if $q^{2} = 10C^{2}$)

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force on free charged particle,&

$F = \dfrac{kq^{2}}{\left(d + x\right)2} - \dfrac{kq^{2}}{ \left($d - x\right)2}$

$F = - kq^{2}\left[\dfrac{4dx}{ \left(d^{2} - x^{2}\right)2}\right]

$a = - \dfrac{4kq^{2}d}{m}\left(\dfrac{x}{d4})$

$a = - \left(\dfrac{4kq^{2}}{md^{3}}\right)$x$

So, angular frequency~

\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{4kq^{2}}{md^{3}}}

\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{4 \times 9 \times {10}^{9} \times 10}{1 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {1}^{3}}}

\omega =$6 $\times {10}^{8}$rad\sec^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: An electron is moving under the influence of the electric field of a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet $S$ having surface charge density $+ \sigma$. The electron at $t = 0$ is at a distance of $1m$ from $S$ and has a speed of $1ms^{- 1}$. The maximum value of $\sigma$, if the electron strikes $S$ at $t = 1s$ is $\alpha\left[\dfrac{m{ϵ}_{0}}{e}\right]\dfrac{C}{m2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The value of the electric field due to the uniformly charged plane sheet is given by

$E = \dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} . . . \left(1\right)$

Thus, the force on the electron is given by

$\begin{cases}F & = & - eE \\ & = & - \dfrac{\sigmae}{2{ε}_{0}} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$$

So, the acceleration of the electron is given by

$a = - $\dfrac{\sigmae}{2{ε}_{0}m}

Given, $u = 1ms^{- 1}$, $t = 1s and $S = - 1m$

Using the equation of motion, it can be written that

$- 1 = 1 \times1 - $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{\sigmae}{2{ε}_{0}m} \times ($1{)}^{2} ⇒ \sigma $==8\dfrac{{ε}_{0}m}{e}Cm^{- 2}$

$∴ $\alpha =$8$.

$

questions.q: A long cylindrical volume contains a uniformly distributed charge of density $ρCm^{- 3}$. The electric field inside the cylindrical volume at a distance $x = \dfrac{2{ε}_{0}}{ρ}m$ from its axis is _____~$Vm^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, Volume charge density& $= ρCm^{- 3}$.

Consider a Gaussian cylindrical surface of height~$h$~and radius~$x$.

Let~$q$~charge is enclosed by the cylinder of radius~$x$.

From Gauss's law,

$∫ E d Scos0 = \dfrac{q}{ε0}$

Here,~$q =$volume charge density$\times$volume of imaginary cylinder.

~$⇒ E\left(2\pixh\right) = \dfrac{ρ \times \pix^{2}h}{ε0}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{ρx}{2{ε}_{0}}$

$⇒ E = \dfrac{ρ}{2{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{2{ε}_{0}}{ρ} = 1$

Thus, electric field is~$1Vm^{- 1}$.
